options.text: Approval process and flow with a scheduled path
Schedule-triggered flow with Submit for Approval action
Approval process with a record triggered flow

sourceExplanation: The correct answer is D. Approval process with a record-triggered flow. Salesforce does not provide a simple "approval before delete" button behavior by default. The practical declarative pattern is to use an Approval Process for manager permission and a record-triggered Flow to automate the submit/delete logic. Flow includes a Submit for Approval action for Classic Approval Processes and also supports deleting records through the Delete Records element. Why not the others: A two-step approval process only handles approval routing; it does not complete the deletion automation by itself. A scheduled path or schedule-triggered flow is not appropriate because this is based on a user's delete request, not a time-based batch process.

stem: Universal Containers manages leads in a Lead qualification queue where Sales reps can accept ownership of the Lea Campaign members are required to Have a sales owner. Which validation rule should an app builder configure?
sourceExplanation: The correct validation rule is: AND( ISNEW(), ISBLANK(Lead.Owner:User.Id) ) This rule prevents a new Campaign Member from being created when the related Lead does not have a User as owner. Leads can be owned by either a user or a queue, and Salesforce queues can own Lead records. Salesforce validation rules block a save when the formula evaluates to True. The ISNEW() function checks whether the record is being created, and ISBLANK() checks whether the Lead owner's User Id is empty. For owner fields in cross-object formulas, Salesforce requires being explicit about the owner type, such as Owner:User or Owner:Queue . Why not others: A is wrong because Lead.Owner.Id is normally populated whether the owner is a user or queue. B and D focus on queue ownership, but the best exam answer checks that the Lead has an actual User owner when the Campaign Member is created.

stem: Ursa Major Solar (UHS) uses a public sharing model for accounts. UHS would like to move to a more restrictive sharing model but wants the Sales team to continue to have access to all account records with the sales record type. Which two actions should an app builder complete to implement this change? Choose 2 answers
sourceExplanation: The correct answers are B. Create a criteria-based sharing rule and C. Update the organization-wide defaults. To move from a public sharing model to a more restrictive model, the app builder must first update the Organization-Wide Defaults for Accounts. OWDs define the baseline record access for users. Then, because the Sales team must still access all Account records with the Sales record type, the app builder should create a criteria-based sharing rule using record criteria, such as Record Type. Salesforce sharing rules are used to extend access when the OWD is Private or Public Read Only. A is incorrect because owner-based sharing rules share records based on owner, not record type. D is incorrect because profiles control object permissions, not record-level access by record type.

stem: The Director of Marketing at Northern Trail Outfitters wants the app builder to create a Formula field that tracks how many days have elapsed since a contact was sent a Marketing communication. The director is only interested in whole units. Which function should be used to return a date for calculating the difference?
sourceExplanation: The correct answer is A. TODAY(). The formula needs to calculate how many whole days have elapsed since a marketing communication was sent. The TODAY() function returns the current date as a Date value, which is appropriate for whole-day calculations. Salesforce documentation also shows that TODAY() can be used with addition and subtraction operators for date calculations. NOW() returns a Date/Time value and can introduce fractional day/time calculations. DATEVALUE() converts a Date/Time or text value into a Date, but the question asks which function should return today's date for calculating elapsed days. DATETIMEVALUE() returns a Date/Time value, not the desired whole- date calculation.

stem: The Cloud Kicks (CK) sales team is currently using a sales app in Lightning Experience. CK is planning a Salesforce mobile app rollout next month to increase productivity for reps while out in the field. After reviewing the mobile app, the sales operations manager asks about ways to create an enhanced user experience. Which two solutions could an app builder suggest? Choose 2 answers

options.text: Allow mobile users to support Account Upstream Agent Closets.
Include Today as a guide from in line size.
Set up different mobile menu configurations of different types of users.
Create a custom app page and Assign to the mobile menu.

sourceExplanation: The correct solutions are D. Create a custom app page and assign it to the mobile menu and B. Include Today as a navigation item in the app. Salesforce supports creating a mobile app page with Lightning App Builder for the Salesforce mobile app. This allows an app builder to design a mobile-focused experience and make it available through mobile navigation. Salesforce also provides Today in the mobile app to help users manage their day, prepare for meetings, and access relevant mobile productivity information. Salesforce documentation states that users access Today from the Salesforce mobile app navigation menu, and admins can add Today to Lightning app navigation and the Mobile Only app. C is not the best verified exam answer for the standard version of this question. While mobile navigation can be customized, the stronger Platform App Builder mobile UX recommendations here are adding a custom mobile app page and adding Today as a navigation item.

stem: A Platform App Builder created a scheduled flow that runs at midnight to perform data cleanup. The flow is designed to query all open Opportunities that haven't been worked for more than 60 days and update the Status field to Closed Lost. However, the app builder notices that the flow is running into governor limits during execution. What is the reason for this?

options.text: The app builder did not specify an object and filter criteria in the Start element of the schedule-triggered flow.
The app builder did not create a Fault Path on the Update Records element.
The flow contains a Loop element that contains an Update Records element inside it.
Schedule-triggered flows do not support updates to standard objects like Opportunities.

sourceExplanation: Performing Data Manipulation Language operations such as Update Records inside a Loop is a classic Flow governor-limit anti-pattern. Each loop iteration can perform another database operation, rapidly consuming transaction limits when a large collection of Opportunities is processed. Salesforce ' s official Flow guidance explicitly says never to place DML operations inside loops. Instead, the app builder should iterate through the records, use Assignment elements to modify them and add them to a record collection, and perform one bulk Update Records operation after the loop. Fault paths improve error handling but do not prevent governor-limit consumption. Schedule-triggered flows can update standard objects, so D is incorrect. The scalability problem described is therefore directly caused by performing Update Records repeatedly inside the Loop element.

stem: Northern Trail Outfitters (NTO) has created the custom objects Trail and Park in Salesforce to track parks and trails respectively. NTO wants to track the total number of trails a park has on the park record without writing any code. Which two actions should an app builder take to accomplish this requirement? Choose 2 answers

options.text: Use a master-detail relationship between the Park and Trail objects.
Use a lookup relationship between the Park and Trail objects.
Use a roll-up summary field on the Park record to show the total number of trails.
Use a formula field on the Park record to show the total number of trails.

sourceExplanation: The correct answers are A. Use a master-detail relationship between the Park and Trail objects and C. Use a roll-up summary field on the Park record to show the total number of trails . To show the total number of child Trail records on the parent Park record without code, the app builder should use a roll-up summary field . Salesforce documentation states that roll-up summary fields display values on a master record based on related detail records. That means Park should be the master object and Trail should be the detail object. Then a roll-up summary field on Park can count the related Trail records. B is incorrect because standard lookup relationships do not support roll-up summary fields. D is incorrect because a formula field cannot count multiple child records.

stem: The VP of sales at AW Computing would like a Roll-Up Summary field onThe Account object to aggregate the amount of opportunities related to an Account. The app builder is unable to implement this change. Why is the app builder unable to fulfill the request?

options.text: The default currency is not an active currency in the organization.
The organization has Advanced Currency Management enable
Roll-Up Summary fields are unavailable on the Account object.
Currency fields are unable to be referenced in Roll-Up Summary fields.

sourceExplanation: The correct answer is B. Salesforce supports roll-up summary fields for summarizing related records, including scenarios involving Account and related Opportunity values. However, Salesforce documentation states that if Advanced Currency Management is enabled, currency roll-up summary fields are invalid when they are on Accounts and summarize Opportunity values. Because the VP wants to aggregate Opportunity Amount values on Account, the app builder cannot create that roll-up summary field if Advanced Currency Management is enabled. Why not others: A is not the stated Salesforce limitation. C is wrong because roll-up summary fields are available on Account in supported scenarios. D is wrong because currency fields can be used in roll-up summaries generally; the issue is specifically Advanced Currency Management with Account-to-Opportunity currency rollups.

stem: Cloud Kicks has a sales rep who is stating that their Contact is unavailable for other users to see within Salesforce. In which three ways can an app builder troubleshoot this issue? Choose 3 answers

options.text: Review the Contact record and ensure it is linked to an Account.
Create a new Contact and have the users try again.
Verify the users with the issue have access to the Contact object.
Create an Account Sharing Rule to give the users access to all records.
Confirm whether Default Organization-Wide Sharing Settings provide access to the Account.

sourceExplanation: The correct answers are A. Review the Contact record and ensure it is linked to an Account, C. Verify the users with the issue have access to the Contact object, and E. Confirm whether Default Organization-Wide Sharing Settings provide access to the Account. A Contact that is not linked to an Account is treated as a private contact. Salesforce states that contacts without an account are private regardless of the sharing model, so checking whether the Contact is associated with an Account is a valid troubleshooting step. Users also need object-level access to the Contact object. Object permissions control whether users have base- level access such as read, create, edit, and delete for an object. Finally, Contact visibility is often affected by Account access, especially when Contact sharing is controlled by the parent Account. Organization-Wide Defaults define the default record access users have for records they do not own, so checking the Account OWD is also correct. B is incorrect because creating a new Contact does not troubleshoot the actual sharing/security issue . D is incorrect because creating a broad Account Sharing Rule for all records is not the first troubleshooting step and may overexpose data.

stem: Sales Managers want to be automatically notified any time there is a change to an Opportunity Close Date and want these changes to be tracked on the Opportunity. Which two configurations should an app builder recommend? Choose 2 answers

options.text: Use a record-triggered flow on Opportunity and a Chatter post action.

sourceExplanation: The correct answers are A. Enable Feed Tracking on Opportunities and D. Use a record-triggered flow on Opportunity and a Chatter post action. Feed Tracking is the correct configuration to track field changes on the Opportunity record feed. Salesforce states that feed tracking detects changes to tracked record fields and posts updates to the feed for users who follow the record. Salesforce also allows admins to enable feed tracking for an object and select tracked fields. A record-triggered flow with a Chatter post action handles the automatic notification requirement. The flow can detect when the Opportunity Close Date changes and post to Chatter, such as mentioning the sales manager or a manager group. Salesforce supports posting to a record's Chatter feed through automation when feed tracking is enabled. B is incorrect because an outbound message sends data to an external endpoint, not a manager notification on the Opportunity. C is incorrect because Historical Trending is mainly for reporting on changes over time, not automatic manager notification on the record.

stem: An app builder needs to deploy a new account detail page layout from Sandbox to production. Which three components should an app builder include in the Change Set to ensure it Deploys successfully and visually as expected? Choose 3 answers
sourceExplanation: The correct answers are A. Detail page layout, B. Custom actions, and D. Custom fields. To deploy a new Account detail page layout successfully and make it look the same in production, the change set must include the actual page layout plus the components used on that layout. Salesforce page layouts control the arrangement of fields, actions, buttons, and related lists on record detail pages. Therefore, if the layout uses new custom fields or custom actions, those components must also exist in production or be included in the change set. Salesforce change set guidance also notes that custom fields must be added individually when deploying customizations. C). System administrator profile is not required just to deploy the visual layout. Profiles are only relevant if deploying access settings or layout assignments. E). Lightning App Builder is not the component needed for a standard detail page layout; a Lightning Record Page would be a different metadata component.

stem: An app builder at DreamHouse Realty created a custom object which has Fields containing data from two different objects via related lookups. What is needed to create "with" or "without" reports on the new custom Object?
sourceExplanation: The correct answer is D. Custom Report Type. A custom report type defines which records and fields are available in a report based on relationships between a primary object and related objects. Salesforce also references custom WITH or WITHOUT report types for reporting on related records. Because DreamHouse Realty needs "with" or "without" reports involving a custom object and related lookup data, the app builder must create a Custom Report Type and define the object relationships. Why others are incorrect: A). Report Filters filter report results but do not define the reportable object relationship. B). Row-Level Formula calculates values per row; it does not create with/without relationship reporting. C). Report Bucket Field groups report values; it does not define related-object report structure.

stem: Uras Major Solar wants to create a relationship between the standard Contact object and a custom Solar Project object. Contacts can potentially be related to multiple Solar Project objects, and a Solar Project can have multiple Contacts associated with it. How should an app builder configure the data model?

options.text: One Master-detail relationship on Contact and one Master-detail relationship on Solar Project
Two Lookup relationships on a new custom object
Two Master-detail relationships on a new custom object
One Lookup relationship on Contact and one Lookup relationship on Solar Project

sourceExplanation: The correct answer is C. Two Master-detail relationships on a new custom object. This is a many-to-many relationship: one Contact can be related to many Solar Projects, and one Solar Project can be related to many Contacts. Salesforce's standard declarative design for many-to-many relationships is a junction object. A junction object is a custom object with two master-detail relationships connecting the two related objects. A is incorrect because the two master-detail relationships belong on the new junction object, not directly on Contact and Solar Project. B can technically relate records, but it is not the standard Salesforce many-to-many model tested here. D does not correctly create a scalable many-to-many model.

stem: Universal Containers wants to track installation information once a Container has been purchased on a custom object. Sales reps should have visibility of All the installations associated with their opportunities. Which kind of relationship should this new object have to Opportunity?
sourceExplanation: Salesforce requires installation records to be directly associated with Opportunities, and sales reps need visibility of all installations tied to their Opportunities. A Master-Detail relationship is the correct solution because: * The Installation object (detail) inherits sharing and security from the Opportunity (master), ensuring sales reps see only their related installations. * Enables roll-up summaries on Opportunity if needed. Salesforce documentation confirms that Master-Detail relationships provide parent-controlled ownership and access, making them ideal for enforcing related record visibility. (Salesforce Help) * B. Hierarchical is only available for User object. * C. Many-to-Many requires a junction object; not needed here. * D. Lookup allows optional, independent access; would not automatically enforce visibility.

stem: Cloud Kicks works on an annual subscription model. When a sales rep marks An opportunity as closed won, a new opportunity should automatically be created for The renewal. The contracts team works outside of Salesforce but also needs to be Notified about closed deals in order to initiate the contract process with the customer. Which automation solution would meet these requirements?
sourceExplanation: The correct answer is C. A record-triggered flow can run automatically when an Opportunity is updated to Closed Won, create a renewal Opportunity, and notify the contracts team. Salesforce Trailhead explains that record-triggered flows are built around trigger, criteria, and action; for example, when an Opportunity is created or updated and meets criteria, the flow can create another record. Salesforce Flow can also create records and send emails, which fits both requirements: create the renewal Opportunity and notify an external contracts team. Why others are incorrect: A Approval Process is for review/approval routing. B Outbound Message may notify an external system, but it does not handle the full renewal Opportunity creation requirement by itself. D Validation Rule only prevents bad data; it does not create records or send notifications.

stem: Cloud Kicks has three types of customer support processes: Platinum, Diamond, and Bronze. The Platform App Builder created separate record types for each process on the Case object. The customer support team should be unable to create new Cases with the Bronze record type. How should the app builder meet this requirement?

options.text: Create a permission set group for Case that includes the Platinum and Diamond record types.
Update the organization-wide defaults to Private for Case.
Update the support team's profile to remove the Bronze record type.
Make the record type hidden to support users and update sharing rules to Private.

sourceExplanation: Record type availability determines which record types a user can select when creating records. Salesforce allows record types to be assigned through profiles, permission sets, and permission set groups. Therefore, if the support team ' s profile currently provides access to Bronze, removing Bronze from that profile prevents users from selecting that record type, assuming it is not granted through another permission set. Organization- wide defaults and sharing rules regulate access to records after they exist; they do not control which record types a user can select during creation. A permission set group containing Platinum and Diamond could grant additional access but does not inherently revoke Bronze access already provided by the profile. The direct solution described by the options is therefore to remove the Bronze record type assignment from the support team ' s profile.

stem: A company wants to prevent sales users from saving Opportunity Products with discounts over 15% for Opportunity records. How should the company configure this requirement?

options.text: Validation rule on the Opportunity Product record
Approval process triggered by Opportunity Product updates
Validation rule on the Opportunity record
Big Deal alert for the Opportunity record

sourceExplanation: The validation belongs on the Opportunity Product because the discount being restricted is a value associated with each individual product line. A validation rule evaluates the record being saved and prevents the transaction when its formula evaluates to TRUE. Therefore, the rule can evaluate the Opportunity Product discount and generate an error whenever it exceeds 15%. Putting the validation on Opportunity would target the parent record rather than the specific line item where the invalid value occurs. An approval process is unnecessary because the requirement is to prevent the save, not route an exception for managerial approval. A Big Deal Alert applies to large Opportunities and is unrelated to product-level discount enforcement. Salesforce recommends validation rules for enforcing record-level business data requirements before save.

stem: An app builder wants to configure a sandbox environment for users to perform user acceptance testing of the latest features from developers. The sandbox should include about 500MB worth of data configured via a template. Also, the sandbox should be refreshed weekly. Which sandbox meets the requirements?
sourceExplanation: The correct answer is D. Partial Copy sandbox. A Partial Copy sandbox is designed for testing and UAT when users need a subset of production data. Salesforce states that Partial Copy sandboxes include metadata plus a subset of production data via sandbox template, support 5 GB data storage, and have a 5-day refresh interval, which satisfies a weekly refresh requirement. A). Full sandbox is incorrect because it copies all production data and has a longer refresh interval. B/C. Developer or Developer Pro are incorrect because they do not copy production data through a template in the same way required for this UAT scenario. ========

stem: At Universal Containers, a Platform App Builder is building a record-triggered flow on Opportunity. When a new Opportunity is created, the flow must set the Stage field to a default value based on the related Account's Industry. The app builder wants the most efficient configuration. Which flow configuration should the app builder use?

options.text: An after-save record-triggered flow with an Assignment element that sets the Opportunity Stage based on Record.Account.Industry.
A before-save record-triggered flow with an Assignment element that sets the Opportunity Stage based on Record.Account.Industry.
An after-save record-triggered flow with an Update Records element that sets the Opportunity's Stage based on the Account's Industry.
A before-save record-triggered flow with an Update Records element that sets the Opportunity's Stage based on the Account's Industry.

sourceExplanation: A before-save record-triggered flow is Salesforce ' s most efficient declarative architecture when the only requirement is to update fields on the record that triggered the flow. Salesforce recommends before-save flows for these updates because changes are applied before the record is committed and do not require a second database save. The flow can reference the related Account ' s Industry and use an Assignment element to place the required default value in the triggering Opportunity ' s Stage field. Salesforce notes that changes made directly to $Record are persisted automatically, so a separate Update Records element is unnecessary. An after-save flow would work but introduce an additional database operation. Therefore, B provides the optimal Fast Field Updates pattern for this requirement.

stem: Universal Containers wants to control the visibility of a specific section of a Lightning page based on the device type used by the user. What should a Platform App Builder recommend?
sourceExplanation: Current Salesforce functionality makes D. Dynamic Forms the appropriate declarative answer. Lightning App Builder supports visibility rules on Dynamic Forms Field and Field Section components, and Salesforce specifically documents device-based visibility through the Device context. An app builder can therefore configure a section to appear for the required form factor, such as phone or desktop, without developing a custom Lightning Web Component. Record Types determine business processes, picklist availability, and layout assignments; they are not device-detection mechanisms. Traditional Page Layouts likewise do not provide device-specific section visibility. A custom LWC could implement custom form-factor behavior programmatically, but it is unnecessary when Dynamic Forms provides native declarative visibility controls. This is a correction to the PDF answer key, which lists B.

stem: Sales reps at Cloud Kicks (CK) forget to submit for approval when CK needs orders reviewed before close won. CK wants to automatically submit Opportunities into the Secure Commitment Stage to eliminate manual submission. Which feature meets the business requirements?

options.text: Record-Triggered flow optimized for Actions and Related Records
Record-Triggered flow optimized for Fast Field Updates

stem: An app builder at Universal Containers has been asked to add The Chatter feed to a custom object record page. Which approach should the app builder use?

options.text: Add a custom Chatter feed component.
Add the standard related list component
Add the standard Chatter feed component.
Add the Chatter feed component from the AppExchange.

sourceExplanation: The correct answer is C. Add the standard Chatter feed component. To add Chatter feed functionality to a custom object Lightning record page, the app builder should use the standard Chatter component in Lightning App Builder. Salesforce documentation states that the Feed component was renamed Chatter in Lightning App Builder and is used to place the publisher and feed combination on a record page. A is incorrect because no custom Chatter feed component is required. B is incorrect because related lists do not add the Chatter feed. D is incorrect because the standard Chatter component is already available; an AppExchange component is unnecessary.

stem: Universal Containers wants to embed a chart of all related Opportunities, by stage, on the Account detail page. Which type of report should an app builder create to add to the Account page layout?

options.text: A tabular report on the Opportunity object
A tabular report on the Account object
A summary report on the Opportunity object
A summary report on the Account object

sourceExplanation: To embed a chart on the Account detail page showing related Opportunities by Stage, the report must summarize Opportunities, not just list them. Salesforce documentation specifies that summary reports allow grouping by fields (e.g., Stage) and can be used in Report Chart components. (Salesforce Help) * Tabular reports cannot be grouped and therefore cannot provide the aggregated chart needed. * The report must be built on the Opportunity object because the records being summarized are Opportunities, not Accounts.

stem: Universal Containers ' 24/7 support requires a guided wizard to step customer service reps through a standardized troubleshooting script. The process must capture user input at various stages and create a follow- up Case record upon completion. Which type of flow should the Platform App Builder build to provide this interactive user interface?
sourceExplanation: A Screen Flow is Salesforce ' s interactive flow type and is specifically intended to guide users through a business process while collecting input. The app builder can create multiple Screen elements representing troubleshooting steps, display instructions and questions, store the representative ' s responses, and then use Create Records to generate the follow-up Case at the end of the process. Salesforce explicitly distinguishes Screen Flows from background automation because Screen Flows require user interaction and support screens, choices, and other interactive components. Schedule-triggered, record-triggered, and platform event- triggered flows execute automatically in the background and therefore do not provide the required multi-step wizard interface. The combination of guided navigation, data capture, and record creation makes Screen Flow the appropriate declarative solution.

stem: At Universal Containers, two record-triggered flows run after an Opportunity is updated. One calculates a custom discount amount, and the other sends an email notification that references the calculated discount. The Platform App Builder must guarantee that the discount-calculation flow runs before the notification flow, while keeping the two flows separate for ownership reasons. How should the app builder meet this requirement?

options.text: Configure the notification flow to run asynchronously after the save so it executes after other record- triggered flows on Opportunity.
Add a scheduled path with a zero-minute interval at the start of the notification flow to delay its execution.
Move both flows ' logic into a single before-save record-triggered flow on Opportunity to control execution order natively.
Set the trigger order in Flow Trigger Explorer for each flow so the discount-calculation flow has a lower trigger order value than the notification flow.

sourceExplanation: Flow Trigger Explorer is specifically designed to manage the execution sequence of record-triggered flows for the same object and trigger category. Salesforce documents that changing a flow ' s order in Flow Trigger Explorer changes its Trigger Order value, and that this value determines the sequence in which applicable flows execute. Therefore, the discount calculation flow should receive the earlier/lower trigger order and the notification flow the later order. This preserves separate flows while guaranteeing deterministic sequencing. An asynchronous path does not provide the same explicit ordering contract. A zero-minute scheduled path unnecessarily changes transaction timing. Combining both flows violates the stated ownership requirement and is not necessary because Salesforce provides native trigger-order controls. The correct Platform App Builder solution is therefore Flow Trigger Explorer.

stem: Which two places can an app builder go to see a list of available Custom Lightning Components in their org? Choose 2 answers
sourceExplanation: The correct answers are C. Lightning App Builder and D. Lightning components in Setup. In Lightning App Builder, custom Lightning components that are configured for use in Lightning App Builder appear in the Lightning Components pane. In Setup # Lightning Components, Salesforce allows admins to view a list of Lightning Web Components and Aura components in the org. Why others are incorrect: A). Visualforce components in Setup lists Visualforce custom components, not Lightning components. B). Salesforce Optimizer App analyzes org configuration and recommendations; it is not the place to list available custom Lightning components.

stem: At Ursa Major Solar, there is a single Lightning record page for the Celestial Bodies custom object; however, there is a Lightning component the App builder wants to restrict to mobile app users. Which feature in the Lightning app builder should be utilized?
sourceExplanation: The correct answer is D. Component visibility filter. In Lightning App Builder, component visibility rules can control whether a component appears based on context, including the device/form factor. Salesforce Trailhead specifically describes creating a visibility rule so a component appears only when the page is viewed on a phone, which matches restricting a Lightning component to mobile users. A is incorrect because form factor settings are generally used for page/device availability or preview behavior, not the best feature for hiding or showing one specific component on a single Lightning record page. B and C are incorrect because the Highlights Panel and Related List Quick Links are page components, not conditional visibility tools.

stem: Cloud Kicks is redefining its entire business process to convert the Manager Notes field from a long text area field The goal is to encourage Managers to be more concise in their comments and stay at 255 characters or less. There is preexisting information in the Manager Notes field that often is well beyond the character limit. What would happen to any existing information if the app builder tries to convert a preexisting long text area field to text area?

options.text: Preexisting information will truncate to the first 255 characters.
Preexisting information will cause an error message to pop up.
Preexisting information will remain even if it was over 255 characters.
Preexisting information in the field will be completely lost.

sourceExplanation: Existing data will be truncated to the first 255 characters. Salesforce documentation on changing custom field types states that when a Long Text Area field is converted to Email, Phone, Text, Text Area, or URL, the record data is truncated to the first 255 characters. Since the target is a standard Text Area with a 255-character limit, longer Manager Notes values would not remain intact. Why not the others? Salesforce does not preserve values beyond the new limit in this conversion. The data is not completely lost, but anything after the first 255 characters is removed.

stem: Cloud Kicks (CK) wants to set up a custom child object to track gift cards issued to a customer. A key requirement is to track the total number of gift cards opened and gift cards issued on an Account. CK wants to permanently ensure the gift cards are unable to be moved across any other Account once it is created. On the gift card object, which field type should be created to support this requirement?
sourceExplanation: The correct answer is B. Master-detail relationship. Cloud Kicks needs two things: count Gift Card records on the Account and prevent Gift Cards from being moved to another Account after creation. A master-detail relationship supports both requirements. First, master-detail enables a roll-up summary field on Account to count related Gift Card records. Salesforce documentation confirms that roll-up summaries work from detail records up to the master record. Second, master-detail relationships prevent reparenting by default. Salesforce documentation states that records cannot be reparented in master-detail relationships by default, although admins can allow reparenting if they choose. A is incorrect because a lookup relationship does not support standard roll-up summary fields and does not permanently lock the parent Account by default. C is incorrect because roll-up summary is a field on the parent Account, not the relationship field type on Gift Card. D is incorrect because a formula cannot count related child records or enforce parent locking.

stem: A sales manager has noticed that reps continue to input contacts Directly in their phone instead of adding them to Salesforce. What should an app builder recommend to ensure the data makes it into Salesforce?

options.text: Allow Salesforce to import Contacts from mobile device Contact lists.
Enable in-app notifications every time a contact is create
Enable ofline create, edit, and delete in Salesforce for Android and iOS.
Allow users to relate a contact to multiple accounts.

sourceExplanation: The correct answer is A. Allow Salesforce to import Contacts from mobile device Contact lists. Salesforce supports importing contacts from a mobile device contact list into Salesforce from the Salesforce mobile app using Import from Device. Salesforce also notes that users need the permission Allow Salesforce to import Contacts from mobile device Contact lists to use this feature. Why others are incorrect: B only notifies users; it does not move phone contacts into Salesforce. C helps users create/edit records offline in Salesforce, but it does not import contacts already entered in the phone's contact list. D is for account-contact relationship modeling, not mobile contact capture.

stem: Northern Trail Outfitters wants the field sales team to only see the accounts that they Own. Separate North American and European marketing teams should only see Accounts in their respective regions. The inside sales team needs to see all accounts In Salesforce. How can this be accomplished?

options.text: Set the Organization-Wide Default to Public for accounts. Create profiles for each marketing team, and create an Inside Sales Team role that is at the top of the Role Hierarchy.

Set the Organization Wide Default to Public for accounts. Create criteria-based sharing rules for Each marketing team, and create an Inside Sales Team permission set with the "View All" setting for Accounts.
Set the Organization-Wide Default to Private for accounts. Create permission sets for each marketing Team, and create an Inside Sales Team profile with the "View All" setting for accounts.

Set the Organization Wide Default to Private for accounts. Create criteria-based sharing rules for Each marketing team, and create an Inside Sales Team profile with the "View All" setting for Accounts.

sourceExplanation: The correct answer is D. Set the Organization-Wide Default to Private for accounts. Create criteria-based sharing rules for each marketing team, and create an Inside Sales Team profile with the "View All" setting for Accounts. The field sales team should only see Accounts they own, so Account OWD must be Private. Salesforce OWDs define users' default access to records they do not own. North American and European marketing teams need access by region, so use criteria-based sharing rules based on the Account region. Salesforce criteria-based sharing rules share records when records match field criteria. Inside sales needs access to all Account records, so give that group View All Records on Account. Salesforce object permissions define that View All Records lets users view all records for that object regardless of sharing settings.

stem: Universal Containers wants to ensure that they are accepting clean data from their users and verify that important fields are entere What should an app builder recommend to meet this requirement?

options.text: Update the important fields to be required on the page layout.
Create a Flow to clean any data that is formatted wrong.
Configure a validation to require a field for a specific record type.
Make a formula field to check the format of the important fields.

sourceExplanation: The correct answer is C. Universal Containers wants to accept clean data and verify that important fields are entered. The best solution is a validation rule, because validation rules verify that data entered by users meets defined standards before the record can be saved. This is stronger than making a field required only on a page layout, because validation rules can enforce requirements based on conditions such as record type. A is weaker because page-layout required fields apply mainly to that UI layout and do not provide the same conditional data-quality enforcement. B is reactive cleanup after bad data exists. D can calculate or display a value, but it does not enforce user data entry by itself.

stem: Universal Containers has a single Contact Lightning record page. A component takes up a lot of room on the page and is NOT needed by users With a Marketing profile. What should the app builder use to solve this issue?
sourceExplanation: Use a Component visibility filter. The issue is not object access or field access. The Contact Lightning record page is shared, but one component should be hidden for users with the Marketing profile. Salesforce Lightning App Builder supports visibility filters on Lightning page components, so the app builder can conditionally show or hide that component based on user/profile criteria. Why not the others? AppExchange is unrelated. Detail page layouts control field layout, not visibility of a Lightning page component. Field-level security controls field access, not whether a large component appears on a Lightning record page.

stem: An app builder wants to update a field on the parent record When a child record connected via lookup is delete Which automation should the app builder use?
sourceExplanation: The correct answer is A. Record-triggered flow. The app builder needs automation to run when a child record is deleted and then update a field on the related parent record. Salesforce states that a record-triggered flow can automatically perform actions when a record is created, updated, or deleted, without user interaction. Autolaunched flow can perform logic, but it does not run automatically on record deletion unless invoked by another automation. Validation rule only prevents invalid data entry. Quick action requires user interaction and is not suitable for automatic updates after deletion.

stem: Universal Containers wants to create a report to show job applications with or without resumes. Which consideration should the Platform App Builder be aware of when creating the custom report type?

options.text: When a custom or external object is deleted, the report type and reports remain but cause an error when the report is run.
A primary object selection is locked once the custom report type has been saved.
Once the report type has been deployed, it is unable to be deleted.
An app builder is unable to create custom report types for objects they do not have permissions for.

sourceExplanation: The primary object of a custom report type is a fundamental design choice and cannot be changed after the report type is saved. Salesforce explicitly states in both the Enhanced and Legacy Custom Report Type Builder documentation that after saving a custom report type, the selected primary object cannot be changed. The primary object determines the base set of records represented by the report type and controls how additional related objects can subsequently be included. Consequently, the app builder must choose the Job Application object deliberately before saving the report type. Deployment does not permanently prevent a custom report type from being deleted, and the other options do not describe the core configuration limitation being tested. Therefore, B is the documented Platform App Builder consideration.

stem: Universal Containers is excited to launch a new app. The company wants to increase the adoption rate and guide users through different walkthroughs and targeted prompts. What should the Platform App Builder recommend?
sourceExplanation: In-App Guidance is Salesforce ' s native capability for contextual onboarding, feature adoption, prompts, and guided walkthroughs directly inside Lightning Experience. Salesforce documents that administrators can create prompts and walkthroughs, determine the target audience, and specify where and when that guidance appears. Targeted prompts can highlight a specific page element, while walkthroughs connect multiple prompts into a step-by-step guided experience. This aligns directly with Universal Containers ' goals of increasing adoption and guiding users through a newly launched application. A Screen Flow is appropriate when collecting information or executing an interactive business process, but it is not the dedicated adoption feature. Dynamic Actions control which actions appear, while Dynamic Forms controls field and section presentation. Neither provides structured onboarding walkthroughs.

stem: An app builder has downloaded a component from the AppExchange successfully; however, they are unable to add it to the Lightning home page. Which two reasons can be preventing the app builder from being able to add the Custom component? Choose 2 answers

options.text: A custom tab must be created to add custom components to the page with the App Builder.
The component requires a developer permission to add it to the page with the App Builder.
My Domain must be deployed to add custom components to the page with the App Builder.
The component is tagged for record pages instead of home pages and is not ing up in The App Builder.

sourceExplanation: The correct answers are C. My Domain must be deployed and D. The component is tagged for record pages instead of home pages. Salesforce custom Lightning components must be properly configured before they appear in Lightning App Builder. Salesforce Trailhead explains that custom components configured for Lightning App Builder appear in the Lightning Components pane, and the component bundle must be compatible with Lightning App Builder and Lightning pages. C is correct because Salesforce requires My Domain for adding custom Lightning components in Lightning Experience/App Builder scenarios. Salesforce Help notes that users cannot add a custom Lightning component without enabling and deploying My Domain. D is correct because Lightning components must be exposed for the correct page type. A component exposed only for record pages will not appear for a Lightning Home page. Salesforce Developer documentation states that lightning__HomePage enables a component to be used on a Home page, while record-page-only configuration is separate. Why others are incorrect: A is incorrect because a custom tab is not required to add components to a Lightning Home page. B is incorrect because "developer permission" is not the normal reason a downloaded component cannot be added to a Lightning Home page.

stem: Universal Containers uses a custom picklist field Account Region on the Account record. They want this region to be reflected on all related contact records And stay in sync if the value of this field changes on the Account. How should an app builder meet this requirement?

options.text: Create a picklist field called ' Account Region ' on Contact object > Create a Lookup Relationship to Update this field if the Account Region field on the Account is change
Create a formula field on the Contact object > Set the value of the formula to ISPICKVAL (Account. Account_Region_o).
Create a text field called ' Account Region ' on Contact object > Create a Lookup Relationship to Update this field if the Account Region field on the Account is change
Create a formula field on the Contact object > Set the value of the formula to TEXT (Account.Account Region_e).

sourceExplanation: The correct answer is D. Universal Containers wants the Account Region value to appear on related Contact records and stay in sync whenever the Account value changes. A cross-object formula field on Contact is the best declarative solution because it dynamically references the parent Account field. Salesforce Trailhead explains that a cross-object formula can pull information from a parent object through a lookup relationship, such as showing Account information on Contact. Because Account Region is a picklist, the formula must convert the picklist value to text using the TEXT() function. Trailhead gives the same pattern with Account Industry on Contact: TEXT(Account.Industry) . B is incorrect because ISPICKVAL() checks whether a picklist equals a specific text value and returns true /false; it does not display the picklist value. A and C are incorrect because creating a copied field and trying to update it through a relationship is unnecessary when a formula field can stay synchronized automatically.

stem: Properly installing managed packages helps prevent conflicts With customizations made by customers and partners. Which functionality should be used to set up packages?
sourceExplanation: The correct answer is A. Lookup field. Cloud Kicks wants to assign a Customer Service Manager user to an Account in addition to the standard Account Owner. The best field type is a Lookup field to the User object. A lookup field stores a relationship to another record and supports reporting, filtering, and record-level navigation. Salesforce describes lookup relationships as a way to relate two records while keeping the records otherwise independent. A Text field would not create a real user relationship and could cause inconsistent names. A Picklist or Multi- select picklist would require manual maintenance of user names and would not behave like an assigned user reference.

stem: A new app builder on the Cloud Kicks team is getting familiar with the data Model. They want to see how standard objects and custom objects relate. Which functionality should the app builder use to view these relationships?
sourceExplanation: The correct answer is C. Schema Builder. Schema Builder is designed to help app builders visualize the Salesforce data model, including standard objects, custom objects, fields, and relationships. Salesforce Trailhead states that Schema Builder lets users visualize and edit the data model and is useful for understanding complex data models. Object Manager and Fields & Relationships are used to configure individual objects and fields, but they do not provide the same visual relationship map. Lightning App Builder is for page layout and UI configuration, not data-model visualization.

stem: Universal Containers has a Lightning record page that supportsBoth the mobile app and desktop. An app builder has downloaded a custom Lightning component from AppExchange, but users are unable to view the Component on mobile devices.

options.text: The component needs to be activate
The record page template is unable to support mobile devices.
The component has been developed for Desktop Pages.
The record page needs to be activate

sourceExplanation: The correct answer is C. The Lightning record page already supports both mobile and desktop, but the downloaded custom component is not visible on mobile. That points to the component itself, not the page activation. Lightning components must be configured to support the required form factors. Salesforce developer documentation explains that components can be configured for desktop form factor Large, phone form factor Small, or both. So, if the AppExchange component was built only for desktop pages or only supports the large form factor, users cannot view it in the Salesforce mobile app. A and D are incorrect because the issue is not page activation if the page already supports mobile and desktop. B is incorrect because the scenario states the record page supports both mobile app and desktop.

stem: Cloud Kicks (CK) wants to begin socializing and collaborating within Salesforce around Customer accounts to discuss various topics. CK would like all company employees to see these Conversations. Which two features of Chatter would meet CK's business needs? Choose 2 answers

options.text: Set up new public Chatter groups.
Set up new private Chatter groups.
Use Chatter actions to create tasks to complete.
Use post action on the Account object.

sourceExplanation: The correct answers are A. Set up new public Chatter groups and D. Use post action on the Account object. Public Chatter groups support open collaboration where company users can share information in a group feed. Salesforce Chatter groups are designed for teams to share information, files, and discussions. Post action on the Account object allows users to discuss customer accounts directly from the Account record feed. Salesforce Chatter feeds appear on record pages and allow users to follow records and see updates about them. Why others are incorrect: Private Chatter groups are not suitable because CK wants all company employees to see the conversations. Chatter actions to create tasks help assign work, but they do not primarily solve open company-wide collaboration around accounts.

stem: An app builder has created a new report type but users are unable to select It from the Report Type list when making a new report for records they own. What could be causing this issue?

options.text: The report type is in a status of In Development.
Access to the necessary object is unavailable.
The report type is in a status of Deploye
Access to Create and Customize Reports is disable

sourceExplanation: If a new report type is created but users cannot select it, it is usually because the report type status is "In Development". Salesforce only makes report types available in the Report Type list once they are deployed. (Salesforce Help) * B. Access to objects could prevent report creation, but the question assumes the user can create reports on records they own. * C. Deploye is the correct deployed state, which would make the report type selectable. * D. Create and Customize Reports permission is required, but the question specifies users are trying to create the report.

stem: At Northern Trail Outfitters (NTO), a Platform App Builder built a new commission calculation flow and supporting components in a Developer sandbox. Before the change reaches production, the project lead requires sales operations users to validate the calculation against real Opportunity data. NTO has a Full sandbox available. Which deployment plan should the app builder use?

options.text: Deploy the components from the Developer sandbox to production using a change set with the Validate Only option, then conduct User Acceptance Testing (UAT) in production.
Refresh the Developer sandbox from production to bring in real Opportunity data, conduct User Acceptance Testing (UAT) in the Developer sandbox, then deploy to production.
Deploy the components from the Developer sandbox directly to production, then have sales operations users validate in production.
Deploy the components from the Developer sandbox to the Full sandbox, conduct User Acceptance Testing (UAT) in the Full sandbox, then deploy to production.

sourceExplanation: The Full sandbox is the appropriate environment for final User Acceptance Testing when realistic production- scale data is required. Salesforce describes a Full sandbox as a replica of the production organization containing metadata and production data and identifies it as suitable for testing, staging, load testing, and UAT. The app builder should therefore move the developed components from the Developer sandbox to the Full sandbox, allow sales operations users to validate the commission calculations against representative Opportunity data, and deploy to production only after successful testing. Conducting UAT directly in production creates unnecessary operational risk. A Developer sandbox contains metadata but does not automatically contain production data at the required scale. Therefore, D follows the proper Salesforce application lifecycle and testing model.

stem: The Human Resources department at Cloud Kicks uses a custom object, JobApplication__c, to record all job applicant information, including fields for the applicant's current and desired salaries. Any Cloud Kicks user who performs hiring manager functions needs to be able to see all applicants ' salary information. Which tool should the Platform App Builder use to accomplish this?
sourceExplanation: Permission Sets are the appropriate mechanism for granting additional object and field access to users who perform a particular function without changing their base profiles. The app builder can create a permission set for hiring managers that grants the required access to JobApplication__c and Read access to the sensitive salary fields through field-level security. Salesforce specifically recommends permission sets and permission set groups rather than profiles for extending field permissions. Sharing Rules and organization-wide defaults govern record-level access; they do not make fields visible when field-level security hides them. Page Layouts control which fields are placed in the interface but cannot override field-level security. Because salary information represents restricted field-level data that only a designated functional group should see, Permission Sets provide the precise least-privilege solution.

stem: Universal Containers (UC) has several large customers that sell their products through dealers. UC identifies and works with a single individual at each customer and at each dealer. Separate bills are sent to each customer and each dealer. These details need to be stored in a format that clearly displays the business entities and their appropriate representatives. How should an app builder implement these requirements?

options.text: Create both customer and dealer as accounts, create account teams on each account and associate the dealer records with the parent account.
Create a single account record, add each rep as a contact and create a custom dealer object.
Create a single parent record, add each rep as a contact to the parent account and add each dealer as a child record.
Create both customer and dealer as accounts, add each rep as a contact on the corresponding account and create an account hierarchy.

sourceExplanation: The correct answer is D. Create both customer and dealer as accounts, add each rep as a contact on the corresponding account and create an account hierarchy. Universal Containers needs to represent separate business entities because separate bills are sent to each customer and each dealer. In Salesforce, business accounts are used to represent companies or organizations, and contacts represent the people who work for those accounts. Salesforce account hierarchies are used to show relationships between related accounts through the Parent Account field. So the best model is: Customer = Account Dealer = Account Representative at each business = Contact on that Account Customer/dealer relationship = Account Hierarchy A is incorrect because Account Teams represent internal Salesforce users working on an account, not external dealer/customer representatives. B and C are incorrect because they do not correctly represent separate billing entities as separate Accounts.

stem: An app builder needs to modify an existing Process Builder that automates some of the work being done by the sales team. What are three capabilities of Process Builder that improve productivity? Choose 3 answers
sourceExplanation: The correct answers are A. Create a child record, C. Update a related record, and D. Send an email alert. Process Builder was designed to automate repetitive business actions. Salesforce documentation describes Process Builder as a tool for automating tasks, emails, and record updates. Process Builder can improve productivity by performing actions such as: Create a child record - Process Builder can create a record when criteria are met. Update a related record - Process Builder can update the record that started the process or related records. Send an email alert - Salesforce documentation specifically states that a process can send an email by using an email alert. B is incorrect because "Start an additional message" is not a standard Process Builder productivity capability. action. E is incorrect because Process Builder does not delete related records as a standard declarative

stem: Northern Trail Outfitters wants to initiate an automatic daily up of its Salesforce org. Which tool should an app builder recommend for this task?
sourceExplanation: The correct answer is C. AppExchange package. The key word is daily. Salesforce's native Data Export Service supports manual and scheduled exports, but Salesforce documentation states that backup files can be generated manually once every 7 days for weekly export or 29 days for monthly export, depending on edition. That does not meet an automatic daily backup requirement. For daily automated backups, the app builder should recommend a backup solution from AppExchange. Report export is not an org backup, and refreshing a full copy sandbox is not a backup automation tool.

stem: Universal Containers created a ' New Task ' custom action on the Opportunity object. The action was added to all page layouts in the Mobile & Lightning Actions section. Which Lightning component should the app builder add to the layout to Display the action?
sourceExplanation: The correct answer is A. Highlights panel. In Lightning Experience, record actions such as New Task appear in the Highlights Panel area of the Lightning record page. Salesforce documentation explains that the actions in the highlights panel come from the object's page layout, specifically the Salesforce Mobile and Lightning Experience Actions section, unless dynamic actions are enabled. Since the custom action was already added to the Mobile & Lightning Actions section on the page layouts, the app builder must add the Highlights Panel component to display those actions on the Lightning record page. Activities shows activity timeline/composer-related functionality, but it is not where page-layout actions are generally displayed. Related Lists and Related Record do not display the main action bar.

stem: Cloud Kicks is building a Field Generation prompt template in Prompt Builder that populates a custom field on the Contact record page with a paragraph summarizing the Contact's most recent Orders. To ground the prompt in the Contact's related Order data, the Platform App Builder needs to build a flow. Which type of flow should the app builder use?
sourceExplanation: A Template-Triggered Prompt Flow is specifically designed to provide dynamically retrieved Salesforce data and additional logic to Prompt Builder templates. Salesforce states that these flows perform logic and actions that generate output text merged into the associated prompt template. The app builder can retrieve the Contact ' s related Order records, construct appropriate prompt instructions, and pass that grounded context back to the Field Generation prompt template. Salesforce also documents the Add Prompt Instructions element as available specifically in template-triggered prompt flows. A record-triggered flow responds to database changes, while a schedule-triggered flow runs at predefined intervals. A generic autolaunched flow does not provide the dedicated Prompt Builder integration required by the scenario. Therefore, A is the correct flow type for grounding this prompt template.

stem: An app builder at Cloud Kicks has been working on changes to a Custom Shoe Sales app in a sandbox and is ready to deploy their changes to production with a change set. Part of the work included updates to a Permission set. What should the app builder take into consideration when deploying the Change set to production?

options.text: The existing permission set will be completely overwritten.
The deployed permission set will only contain changes related to the change set.
Changes to field-level security in the permission set will not be applie
The deployed permission set will merge with the existing permission set.

sourceExplanation: The correct answer is B. The deployed permission set will only contain changes related to the change set. When permission sets are included in change sets, the deployment carries permission settings related to the components included in the change set. The existing permission set in production is not completely overwritten as a whole object, and field-level security changes can be included when the relevant fields are part of the deployment. Salesforce documents permission sets and profile settings as access settings that can be included with change sets. A is incorrect because the whole permission set is not simply wiped and replaced. C is incorrect because field-level security can be deployed when included properly. D is close in plain language, but the more accurate exam answer is that the deployed permission set contains only changes related to the change set.

stem: Universal Containers wants to dynamically display a component on a Lightning record page for an account based on criteria about the related contact. Which solution should an app builder use to fulfill this requirement?

options.text: Add a related record component to the page layout.
Hide the component behind a tab on the page layout.
Set the filter type on the component visibility to display based on user permissions, using custom Permission to define the dynamic criteria
Set the component visibility to display based on an advanced filter type, using the contact field(s) to Define the dynamic criteria

sourceExplanation: The correct solution is component visibility with advanced filters. Lightning App Builder allows components on Lightning pages to be shown or hidden dynamically based on filter criteria. Salesforce Admin guidance also explains that App Builder filters can customize which components display on record pages and can use field values from related records, running user, and permissions. Because the component must display dynamically based on criteria about the related Contact, the app builder should use an advanced visibility filter using the Contact field criteria. Why not others: A). Related Record component displays related record data but does not solve dynamic visibility by itself. B). Hiding behind a tab does not dynamically control visibility. C). Custom permission controls visibility by user permission, not by related Contact field criteria.

stem: Universal Containers (UC) is launching a new HR Recruitment app and needs to perform User Acceptance Testing (UAT) before deploying to production. This app deals with sensitive data, testing requires realistic data volume, and needs to be tested by actual UC users. Which sandbox should a Platform App Builder recommend for this phase?
sourceExplanation: A Partial Copy sandbox is specifically intended for testing scenarios that need representative production data without requiring an entire production dataset. Salesforce states that Partial Copy sandboxes contain production metadata plus a selected sample of production data defined through a sandbox template and explicitly identifies User Acceptance Testing, integration testing, and training as appropriate uses. The template also lets administrators select the objects required for testing and exclude sensitive or irrelevant data sets when necessary. Developer and Developer Pro sandboxes primarily copy metadata and do not automatically provide representative production data. A Scratch Org is a temporary source-driven development environment rather than the preferred UAT environment for actual business users and realistic production-derived data. Therefore, A is the appropriate sandbox type.

stem: A Platform App Builder at Cloud Kicks is creating a flow approval process for travel requests. The requirement is to assign the approval to a specific user who will be determined at runtime based on other data in the flow. How must the app builder configure the approver for the approval step?

options.text: Use a Formula resource to define the approver directly in the Approver Type field.
Set the Approver Type to "User" and select a specific user from the list.
Set the Approver Type to "Resource" and select the text variable containing the username.
Set the Approver Type to "Queue" and assign the queue that contains the dynamic user.

sourceExplanation: Resource is specifically intended for approvers that must be resolved dynamically at runtime. Salesforce ' s Flow Approval Process documentation defines Resource as an approver type that references a variable containing a user ' s username, a public group ' s API name, or a queue ' s API name. At runtime, the associated orchestration resolves the value and determines the appropriate assignee. Therefore, the app builder should store the dynamically determined username in a text variable and select that resource in the approval step. Selecting User would require choosing a predetermined user while designing the approval process, which does not satisfy the runtime requirement. Queue similarly identifies a configured queue rather than dynamically resolving an individual user. A Formula cannot directly substitute for the Approver Type configuration specified by Salesforce ' s Flow Approval Process model.

stem: Universal Containers requires a standardized project management tracking system to be visible within its existing Salesforce environment. The Platform App Builder decides to browse AgentExchange to find a complete, preconfigured solution that includes custom objects, fields, and automation rules. What should the app builder install from AgentExchange to ensure automatic upgrades to the package?
sourceExplanation: A managed package is designed for distributable Salesforce solutions whose components can be maintained and upgraded by the package provider. Salesforce states that managed packages provide fully upgradeable application resources, and AgentExchange guidance distinguishes them from unmanaged packages by specifically noting that providers can automatically upgrade managed solutions. This makes a managed package appropriate when Universal Containers wants a complete preconfigured application while minimizing ongoing manual maintenance. An unmanaged package provides editable components but does not have the same provider-managed upgrade mechanism; receiving a newer unmanaged version generally requires replacement or reinstallation. A change set transfers metadata between related Salesforce orgs and is not an AgentExchange distribution package. A data kit is not the package type used to deliver an upgradeable Salesforce application.

stem: Universal Containers manages internal projects by department using a custom object called Projects. Only employees in the project's respective department should have view access to all of the department's project records. If an employee changes job roles and moves to another department, the employee should no longer have access to projects within the former department. Which option meets these requirements, assuming the organization-wide default for Projects is set to Private?

options.text: Create a criteria-based sharing rule using the Project's department that grants access to users through Public Groups.
Create a criteria-based sharing rule using the Project's department that grants access to users through Permission Sets.
Create a criteria-based sharing rule using the Project's department that grants access to users through Profiles.
Create a criteria-based sharing rule using the Project's department that grants access to users through Account Teams.

sourceExplanation: A criteria-based sharing rule can identify Project records according to the Department field and share matching records with the appropriate public group. Salesforce documents that criteria-based sharing rules determine which records are shared based on field values and can grant access to public groups. Administrators can therefore maintain departmental public-group membership as employees change roles. When an employee leaves one department, removing that user from its public group removes the sharing path to those departmental Projects after sharing recalculation. Permission sets and profiles control object and field permissions but are not targets for criteria-based record-sharing rules. Account Teams apply specifically to Account collaboration and are unrelated to a custom Project object. With Project OWD set to Private, public groups plus criteria-based sharing provide the required controlled departmental visibility.

stem: Universal Containers (UC) wants to test code against a subset of production data that is under 5 GB Additionally, UC wants to refresh this sandbox every Weeken Which type of sandbox should be used to accomplish this?
sourceExplanation: The correct sandbox type is Partial Copy. A Partial Copy sandbox is built for testing with a subset of production data. Salesforce lists Partial Copy sandboxes with 5 GB data storage and a 5-day refresh interval, which supports the requirement to refresh it every weekend. Why the other options are wrong: Developer and Developer Pro sandboxes are mainly for development and do not copy a produc tion data subset in the same way. A Full sandbox can copy all production data, but its refresh interval is longer and it is unnecessary for a subset under 5 GB.

stem: Cloud Kicks (CK) has a formula field specialty or Opportunity that gets its value from the specialty field on the related Account. CK has changed its processes to allow opportunities to have different values for Specialty than their Account. How can sales reps enter values for the specialty field on Opportunity, while preserving the values on existing opportunities?

options.text: Extent the data, convert the field to GETTING and mount the data.
Convert the field to a text field and the values in the left.
Create a new text field and keep using the existing formula field.
Create a new text field and import the formula field values in it.

sourceExplanation: The correct answer is D. Create a new text field and import the formula field values in it. The existing Specialty__c field is a formula field, so users cannot manually edit it. Formula fields calculate their value automatically from other fields. Since Cloud Kicks now wants Opportunity Specialty__c values to be different from the related Account value, the app builder should create a new editable field, such as a Text field, and then load the existing calculated formula values into that new field for existing Opportunity records. This preserves historical Opportunity values while allowing sales reps to enter or update Specialty values going forward. Salesforce documentation explains that roll-up/formula-style calculated values are system- derived, while changing custom field types has limitations and requires care when data must be preserved. A and B are incorrect because a formula field cannot simply become an editable text field while safely preserving all existing calculated values. C is incomplete because creating a new text field without importing the existing formula values does not preserve the current values on existing Opportunities.

stem: Universal Containers (UC) has several large customers that sell their products through dealers. UC identifies and works with a single individual at each customer and at each dealer. Separate bills are sent to each customer and each dealer. These details need to be stored in a format that clearly displays the business entities and their appropriate representatives. How should an app builder implement these requirements?

options.text: Create a single parent record, add each rep as a contact to the parent account and add each dealer as a child/group.
Create both customer and dealer as accounts, add each rep as a contact to the corresponding account and create an account hierarchy.
Create a single account record, add each rep as a contact and create a custom dealer object.
Create both customer and dealer as accounts, create account teams on each account and associate the dealer records with the parent account.

sourceExplanation: The correct answer is B. Create both customer and dealer as accounts, add each rep as a contact to the corresponding account and create an account hierarchy. Customers and dealers are both separate business entities, and separate bills are sent to each. In Salesforce, business entities are best represented as Accounts, while the single individual at each business should be stored as a Contact under the correct Account. Salesforce account hierarchy is used to show parent-child relationships between related accounts. Why not D? Account Teams represent internal Salesforce users working on an account, not external customer /dealer representation.

stem: Service agents at Ursa Major Solar want a more condensed case view. Service agents also want to be able to modify the associated contact and account Records from the case page layout on the Lightning record page. Which two components should an app builder use to meet these requirements? Choose 2 answers
sourceExplanation: The correct answers are A. Tabs and B. Related record. Tabs help create a more condensed Lightning record page by grouping information into separate tabbed sections instead of showing everything in one long page. Salesforce Lightning App Builder allows app builders to add, remove, reorder, and customize components on Lightning record pages. Related Record is required because service agents want to modify the associated Contact and Account directly from the Case Lightning record page. Salesforce Help states that the Related Record component uses quick action metadata and requires an associated quick action to update records. Why others are incorrect: Path is used to guide users through stages or status values, not to edit related Account or Contact records. Rich Text displays formatted guidance or static text; it does not provide editable related-record functionality.

stem: An app builder is creating a custom object called Testimonial__c and wants to connect Testimonial__c records with both the submitter's Contact record and Account record If the Account is deleted, the Testimonial__c records should also be delete If the Contact is deleted, but the Account remains, the Testimonial__c records should remain. How should this be accomplished?

options.text: Create a lookup relationship from Testimonial_to Account and a master-detail relationship from Testimonial to Contact.
Make Testimonial ca junction object between Account and Contact using master-detail relationships.
Create a master-detail relationship from Testimonial_to Account and a lookup relationship from Testimonial To Contact.
Make both the Contact and Account fields required on the Testimonial object and create lookup relationships from Testimonial_cto Contact and to Account.

sourceExplanation: The correct design is to create a master-detail relationship from Testimonial__c to Account and a lookup relationship from Testimonial__c to Contact. The Account relationship must be master-detail because Salesforce deletes related detail records when the master record is deleted. That matches the requirement that if the Account is deleted, the related Testimonial__c records are also deleted. The Contact relationship must be lookup because the Testimonial__c record must remain when the Contact is deleted. Salesforce lookup relationships can keep the child record and clear the lookup value when the referenced record is deleted. Why the other options are wrong: A reverses the required behavior. B would delete the testimonial if either master side caused deletion behavior, which does not fit the Contact requirement.
